data.narrative:
Climeworks, a Series F climate technology company founded by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher, operates in the Climate & Energy sector alongside a peer set of 9 comparable companies—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. The company has raised in excess of $1.0B to date.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable methodology due to peer-set constraints. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.3x multiplier typical of Series F advancement to the $1.0B total capital raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $1.3B. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable; while 9 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) returned insufficient datapoints to support robust triangulation, and an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B (low) to $1.5B (high), centered at $1.3B. The range reflects typical Series F progression dynamics applied to disclosed capital raised. Key uncertainties stem from the single-method foundation of this analysis: the stage-progression multiplier assumption lacks peer validation, and the absence of a comparable-company cross-check limits confidence in terminal value anchoring. Refinement would require either expanded access to same-stage Climate & Energy financings or public market observable data from peer holdings.
